findings.title: [P1] Skip rejections from superseded (aborted) searches
findings.body: Every `search()` call first aborts the previous request via `this.active?.abort()` (line 21). With standard `AbortSignal` semantics, that aborted in-flight request's promise then rejects — and the new unconditional `catch` routes that deliberate cancellation into `this.renderError(error)`. Trigger: any new search issued while a previous one is still in flight (the normal case in a search/typeahead controller). Consequences: a spurious error is rendered for an intentional cancellation, and if the stale rejection settles after the newer request's `this.render(result)` runs, the stale error overwrites the fresh result. Guard the catch — e.g. skip when `error.name === 'AbortError'` or when the controller is no longer `this.active` — before rendering.

findings.title: [P1] `renderError` is not defined anywhere
findings.body: The added catch calls `this.renderError(error)`, but no `renderError` member exists on `SearchController` or anywhere else in this repository — `src/search.ts` is the only source file, and the class declares no such method. Unlike `active`, `api`, and `render` (referenced before this PR), this reference is newly introduced by this diff. Scenario: any `api.search` rejection — exactly the case this change is meant to handle — makes the catch throw `TypeError: this.renderError is not a function`, masking the original API error instead of rendering it; under TypeScript checking it is also a new missing-property error. Define the member (or otherwise implement the error-render path) before merging.

findings.title: [P2] `search()` now swallows all failures, changing its rejection contract
findings.body: Before this change, the promise returned by `search()` rejected when `api.search` failed, letting callers catch, retry, or report failures. After this change the catch returns normally, so `search()` always resolves (with `undefined`) on the failure path. The PR description states "preserving existing contracts", so this observable contract change deserves an explicit decision: either rethrow errors that should remain the caller's responsibility, or document that all failures are now handled internally via `renderError`. No in-repo callers exist today, so this is non-blocking, but it will silently surprise any caller built against the old contract.
